Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

please keep the setting text straightforward because i may need to explain it to the other people who use the shared work laptop nora said quote please leave the tab open until the receipt appears end quote she was talking about a separate order page and not about this extension preference the relevant pages are all in my saved list and the label print review is how i will find them again after monday i have not decided whether to order the paper yet and the city library repair workshop is only a page i wanted to keep for later the preference i am asking about is still postponing the weekly summary to monday at nine while leaving the other notification controls alone", "output": "I want to postpone the weekly summary from the Fieldnote Clip browser extension until Monday morning because I review saved pages before the first team call. The preference should affect only the summary message and not the small badge that appears on the extension button. I use the extension on a work laptop and a home laptop, and both are signed in to the same account. The work laptop is usually open by eight thirty, while the home laptop stays in my bag until I finish breakfast. The Monday summary should still include pages saved from either device during the previous week. I am not asking to change how pages are captured or how long they remain in the reading list.

On Friday afternoon, I saved a set of supplier pages about paper stock and recycled envelopes. The first page came from the Harbor Supply catalog and had a price table lower down the page. The second was a public notice from the city library about its repair workshop, and the third was a note from our printer with two delivery windows. I added the label print review to all three pages and wrote a short comment on the catalog page about checking the weight before ordering. I want those details to stay in the summary even though I saved them on different days. The extension currently groups pages by the date they were captured and then shows the label beneath each title. That arrangement is useful because the weekly summary is also where I notice a page I forgot to open.

The preference panel is under Account, then Notifications, on the left side of the extension settings page. The summary control is below the daily reminder control and above the browser update notice. I saw the current wording last week, and it said, “Send a weekly summary every Monday at seven thirty.” I would like the time to be nine o’clock instead, and I want to postpone the message until then rather than receive it at seven thirty and move it myself. The browser language is English, and the account time zone is set to Pacific Time. I sometimes travel to the East Coast, but I do not want this preference to follow my location or change the time zone in the account settings.

The preference details are:
1. Postpone the weekly summary from seven thirty to nine o’clock on Monday.
2. Include pages saved on both the work laptop and the home laptop.
3. Keep the existing title, label, and comment for each saved page.
4. Leave the daily reminder and the browser update notice at their current times.

I am mentioning those other controls because they appear close together on the same settings page, and I do not want to confuse them with the weekly summary. The setting should be easy to recognize when I return to the panel next month, and the saved choice should still be visible beside the summary control.

If the work laptop is asleep at nine o’clock on Monday, then send the summary the next time the extension can deliver a notification after the laptop wakes up, but do not send it before nine o’clock on Monday. If the laptop is already awake, then the summary can arrive at nine as usual. I check messages before the team call, but I do not want a notification to appear during the quiet period that runs from ten at night until seven in the morning on any day. This quiet period is already part of my browser notification preferences. The Monday time should not override it when a delayed message becomes eligible.

My colleague Nora asked whether the summary would contain every page saved under the print review label, and I told her it should contain the three pages from Friday and any other pages saved in the same week. I do not mean that the extension should search old weeks for pages with that label. The summary should cover the normal previous week only. If the catalog changes its price table after I save it, I still want the saved page entry and my comment as they were captured. I use the summary as a reminder of what I collected, not as a refreshed copy of each website.

There is one case that may matter later: if I turn off notifications for the whole browser while traveling, keep the postponed Monday summary preference saved rather than clearing it when browser notifications are turned on again. The existing Monday time and the quiet period should still apply. If I change the summary preference myself, I will do that in the same account settings panel. I am not asking for a separate travel schedule, and I do not want the extension to send the weekly message to my colleague or to another email address. The summary is for this account and should remain a browser notification.

Please keep the setting text straightforward because I may need to explain it to the other people who use the shared work laptop. Nora said, “Please leave the tab open until the receipt appears.” She was talking about a separate order page and not about this extension preference. The relevant pages are all in my saved list, and the label print review is how I will find them again after Monday. I have not decided whether to order the paper yet, and the city library repair workshop is only a page I wanted to keep for later. The preference I am asking about is still postponing the weekly summary to Monday at nine while leaving the other notification controls alone."}]
